entries.non_ste_example: Queue the image processing tasks before the worker starts.
entries.ste_example: Add the image processing tasks to the queue before the worker starts.
entries.explanation: "Queue" is a code-domain technical noun (category 18, infrastructure and messaging). P13 forbids using technical nouns as verbs. The STE version uses the approved verb "add" (per P12 synonym table: add) and keeps "queue" as a code-domain technical noun in a prepositional phrase.

entries.non_ste_example: Archive the log files that are older than 30 days.
entries.ste_example: Move the log files that are older than 30 days to the archive.
entries.explanation: "Archive" is a code-domain technical noun (category 18, database and storage terminology). P13 forbids using technical nouns as verbs. The STE version uses the approved verb "move" and keeps "archive" as a code-domain technical noun in a prepositional phrase, paralleling the spec pattern where "oil" must remain a noun.

entries.non_ste_example: The authentication module interfaces with the external OAuth provider.
entries.ste_example: The authentication module connects to the external OAuth provider through an interface.
entries.explanation: "Interface" is a code-domain technical noun (category 17, software architecture and design patterns). P13 forbids using technical nouns as verbs. The STE version uses the approved verb "connect" (per P12 synonym table: connect) and keeps "interface" as a code-domain technical noun. This adapts the spec pattern where technical nouns may not be verbed even in common usage.

entries.non_ste_example: Flag the user accounts that have not verified their email address.
entries.ste_example: Set a flag for the user accounts that have not verified their email address.
entries.explanation: "Flag" is a code-domain technical noun (category 18, configuration and metadata). P13 forbids using technical nouns as verbs. The STE version uses the approved verb "set" (per P12 synonym table: set) and keeps "flag" as a code-domain technical noun with an article. This adapts the spec "oil" pattern — the action is expressed through a general-purpose approved verb.

entries.non_ste_example: Thread the parsing operation to reduce the total execution time.
entries.ste_example: Run the parsing operation in a thread to reduce the total execution time.
entries.explanation: "Thread" is a code-domain technical noun (category 16, computer science and concurrency). P13 forbids using technical nouns as verbs. However, like "drill" in the original spec, "thread" can also be a code-domain technical verb (rule 1.12, category 2c, system operations) when it refers to the act of creating a thread. Both usages are valid in their correct part-of-speech category. The STE version uses the noun form clearly in a prepositional phrase, paralleling the spec "log" dual-category example.
